learn: Syncopation places accents on weak beats or between beats, making music feel bouncy.
Ragtime and jazz use lots of syncopation.
Scott Joplin's "The Entertainer" (1902) is a famous syncopated ragtime piece.
check: Which style uses lots of syncopation?
lessons.try: Listen to "The Entertainer" and clap the bouncy rhythm.

learn: A dotted quarter note gets 1 1/2 beats, often followed by an eighth note.
This pattern appears in songs like "Auld Lang Syne".
Counting "1-and-2-and" helps place notes accurately.
check: A dotted quarter is often followed by an...
lessons.try: Clap a dotted quarter and eighth pattern while counting aloud.

learn: Composers combine note values to build interesting rhythms.
Repetition and variation make rhythms memorable.
Each measure must match the time signature.
lessons.try: Compose an eight-measure rhythm in 4/4 and perform it.

learn: In simple meter, each beat divides into two: 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4.
Marches are often in 2/4; waltzes in 3/4; most pop songs in 4/4.
The bottom number 4 means a quarter note gets one beat.
check: A quarter note gets one beat
In simple meter, beats divide into...
lessons.try: Listen to three songs and decide if they're in 2, 3 or 4.

learn: In compound meter, each beat divides into three: 6/8 is a common example.
6/8 feels like two big beats, each split into three: ONE-two-three, FOUR-five-six.
"Row, Row, Row Your Boat" is in 6/8.
check: In compound meter, beats divide into...
6/8 feels like how many big beats?
"Row, Row, Row Your Boat" is in...
lessons.try: Sway in two while counting six to a 6/8 song.

learn: Some music changes meter, keeping listeners interested.
Composers mark a new time signature where it changes.
Conductors change their patterns to match.
check: Where is a new time signature marked?
lessons.try: Clap two measures of 4/4, then two of 3/4, and repeat.

units.t: Reading Notes on the Treble Staff

learn: Treble lines: E, G, B, D, F. Spaces: F, A, C, E.
Notes above the staff continue the alphabet: G above the top line, then A on a ledger line.
Practise reading quickly by naming notes in random order.
check: The bottom line of the treble staff is...
lessons.try: Name ten random treble staff notes in under 30 seconds.

learn: A key signature at the start of each line shows which notes are always sharp or flat.
G major has one sharp: F♯. F major has one flat: B♭.
C major has no sharps or flats.
check: Which key has no sharps or flats?
lessons.try: Find the key signature in a piece of sheet music.

learn: Sight-reading means playing or singing music you've never seen before.
Before starting, check the clef, key, time signature and tempo.
Keep going even if you make a mistake.
check: If you make a mistake while sight-reading, you...
lessons.try: Sight-sing a simple four-measure melody using note names.

learn: Dynamics range from ppp (extremely soft) to fff (extremely loud).
Subito means suddenly: subito piano means suddenly soft.
Dynamics help shape phrases like a speaker's voice.
lessons.try: Sing a phrase with a crescendo to the middle and a decrescendo to the end.

learn: Accelerando speeds up gradually. Ritardando (rit.) slows down gradually.
A tempo means return to the original speed.
A fermata (𝄐) means hold the note longer than written.
lessons.try: Clap a rhythm with a ritardando and a fermata at the end.

learn: Articulation is how notes are attacked and connected.
A slur connects notes smoothly (legato). A dot above a note means staccato.
An accent (>) means emphasise; a tenuto (–) means hold for full value.
check: A dot above a note means...
lessons.try: Play or sing the same melody with slurs, then staccato.

learn: Popular songs often use verse-chorus form.
Verses tell the story with different words each time. The chorus repeats with the same words.
A bridge is a contrasting section that leads back to the chorus.
check: Which part repeats the same words?
lessons.try: Map the form of a favourite song: verse, chorus, bridge.

learn: The 12-bar blues is a form with 12 measures and a set chord pattern.
It uses the I, IV and V chords.
Many rock, jazz and blues songs follow this form.
check: How many bars in the 12-bar blues?
lessons.try: Count 12 bars while listening to a blues song.

learn: A canon has one melody imitated by other voices starting later, like a round.
Pachelbel's "Canon in D" uses a repeating bass under imitating violins.
A fugue, often by Bach, is a complex form where a theme enters in different voices.
lessons.try: Listen to Pachelbel's "Canon in D" and count how many times the bass pattern repeats in one minute.

learn: String instruments vibrate strings; length, thickness and tension change pitch.
Wind instruments vibrate a column of air; longer tubes make lower notes.
Percussion instruments vibrate when struck; bigger drums sound lower.
lessons.try: Make a straw oboe and cut it shorter to raise the pitch.

learn: The piano is a keyboard instrument where hammers strike strings.
The organ makes sound by pushing air through pipes.
Synthesisers create sounds electronically.
lessons.try: Compare a piano sound and a synthesiser sound in an app.

learn: A concert band has woodwinds, brass and percussion but usually no strings.
A string quartet has two violins, a viola and a cello.
A jazz combo might have piano, bass, drums and a saxophone or trumpet.
check: A concert band usually has no...
lessons.try: List the instruments in a band or ensemble you've heard.

learn: Contour is the overall shape of a melody: rising, falling, arch or wave.
"Joy to the World" begins with a falling scale.
Drawing a melody's contour helps you remember it.
check: "Joy to the World" begins with a...
lessons.try: Draw the contour of a song you know.

learn: An interval is the distance between two pitches.
Seconds are steps, thirds are skips, and fourths or larger are leaps.
"Here Comes the Bride" starts with a fourth; "Twinkle, Twinkle" jumps a fifth.
lessons.try: Sing a third, a fourth and a fifth from do.

learn: A good melody often moves mostly by step with a few leaps.
After a leap, melodies often step back the other way.
End on do (the home note) to sound finished.
lessons.try: Compose an eight-measure melody in C major ending on C.

learn: A chord is built by stacking thirds: C-E-G is a C major chord.
Chords are labelled with Roman numerals: I, IV and V are the most common.
In C major, I = C, IV = F, V = G.
check: In C major, the V chord is...
lessons.try: Play or listen to I-IV-V-I in C major.

learn: Chords can accompany a melody, supporting it with harmony.
Change chords when the melody's notes fit a new chord.
Many folk songs use only I and V chords.
lessons.try: Accompany "Clementine" with I and V chords on a ukulele or keyboard app.

learn: Two-part singing has a melody and a harmony part.
Descants are high harmony parts sung above the melody.
Listen carefully to stay on your part.
check: High harmony part above the melody
Two-part singing has a melody and...
To stay on your part, you...
lessons.try: Sing a melody while someone sings a descant.

learn: Hold the recorder with your left hand on top and right hand below.
Cover holes with the pads of your fingers, not the tips.
Blow gently, like warm air on a window. Use "too" to start notes.
lessons.try: Play a gentle B with your left thumb and first finger.

learn: B: left thumb and first finger. A: add the second finger. G: add the third finger.
Songs like "Hot Cross Buns" use B, A and G.
Keep fingers close to the holes for smooth changes.
check: Which note uses thumb and two fingers on the left hand?
Keep fingers close to the holes for...
lessons.try: Play "Hot Cross Buns" on recorder: B A G, B A G.

learn: Low E, D and C use the right hand too.
High C and D use fewer fingers.
With more notes, you can play songs like "Ode to Joy".
check: With more notes you can play...
lessons.try: Learn high C and play "Mary Had a Little Lamb".

learn: American folk songs include sea shanties, cowboy songs and railroad songs.
"I've Been Working on the Railroad" was sung by workers.
Folk songs tell stories of everyday life.
check: "I've Been Working on the Railroad" was sung by...
lessons.try: Learn the chorus of a traditional work song.

learn: The blues grew from African American spirituals, work songs and field hollers in the South.
Jazz combined blues, ragtime and brass band music in New Orleans.
Louis Armstrong was a famous jazz trumpeter and singer; Duke Ellington led a famous big band.
lessons.try: Listen to Louis Armstrong and describe his voice.

learn: "The Star-Spangled Banner" became the national anthem in 1931; its words were written by Francis Scott Key in 1814.
John Philip Sousa wrote marches like "The Stars and Stripes Forever".
Musical theatre combines songs, dialogue and dance to tell stories.
check: Who wrote the words of "The Star-Spangled Banner"?
Musical theatre combines songs, dialogue and...
lessons.try: Listen to a Sousa march and march to it.
